category: User Language: builtin functions (character, file, math, misc, units)
description: ULP builtin functions, part 1: character classification and case conversion, file handling (fileglob, filename parts, file size/time, fileread, fileerror), mathematical functions, miscellaneous functions (cfgget/ cfgset, country, language, exit, lookup, palette, sleep, sort, status, system, fdlsignature) and the unit conversions between internal units and mm/mil/inch/micron. Source: EAGLE 9.6.0 built-in help.

tools.name: isalnum, isalpha, iscntrl, isdigit, isgraph, islower, isprint, ispunct, isspace, isupper, isxdigit
tools.description: Character classification functions: each returns non-zero if the character belongs to the category and zero otherwise. They cover letters, digits, alphanumerics, hex digits, upper/lower case, white space, control, printable, graphic and punctuation characters, and are typically used when parsing names or text files character by character.

parameters.name: c
parameters.description: The character to test (a char, or a string element s[i]).

tools.notes: Categories: isalnum letters or digits; isalpha A-Z/a-z; iscntrl 0x7F or 0x00-0x1F; isdigit 0-9; isgraph printing characters except space; islower a-z; isprint 0x20-0x7E; ispunct punctuation; isspace space, tab, CR, LF, VT, FF (0x09-0x0D, 0x20); isupper A-Z; isxdigit 0-9, A-F, a-f. They work on single ASCII characters.

tools.name: tolower, toupper
tools.description: Convert a single character to lower or upper case. Only letters of the opposite case are changed; every other character is returned unchanged. For whole strings use strlwr() and strupr().
tools.usage:
char tolower(char c);
char toupper(char c);
tools.notes: See strupr()/strlwr() for converting strings, e.g. for case-insensitive name comparison.

tools.name: fileerror
tools.description: Returns the status of the file I/O operations (output(), printf(), fileread() ...) performed since the previous call: 0 if everything was fine, non-zero if an operation failed. Call it once before the I/O to reset the state and again afterwards to check the result; the user has already been shown an error message when it reports a failure.
tools.notes: Returning a non-zero result via exit() lets a calling script stop when writing failed.

tools.name: fileglob
tools.description: Searches a directory with a wildcard pattern ('*' and '?') and stores the matching names in a string array, returning the number of entries. A pattern ending in '/' lists the whole directory; directory names in the result end with '/', come first and are sorted alphabetically ('.' and '..' are never returned). Use it to process all boards, libraries or scripts of a folder.

parameters.name: array
parameters.description: Receives the matching path names.

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: Directory plus wildcard pattern, e.g. "D:/work/*.brd"; end with '/' to list a directory.

tools.notes: The resulting names always use '/' as directory separator, also on Windows, where a backslash in the pattern is accepted as separator too and sorting is case-insensitive. No match or no permission gives an empty array.

tools.name: filedir
tools.description: Returns the directory part of a file name, including the drive letter on Windows. Typical uses are finding the folder of the current board (B.name) or of the running ULP (argv[0]) to place output files next to them.

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: Full or relative file name.

tools.notes: The shipped ULPs append file names directly to the result (filedir(L.name) + "clear.scr"), i.e. the directory is returned with its trailing separator. filesetext(B.name, ".txt") is often the simpler way to write a file next to the design.

tools.name: fileext
tools.description: Returns the extension of a file name (for example .brd). Use it to branch on file types, such as when processing a list from fileglob() or a name chosen in dlgFileOpen().

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: File name to inspect.

tools.notes: Compare case-insensitively (strlwr) because file systems like Windows accept .BRD.

tools.name: filename
tools.description: Returns the name part of a file path including its extension, without the directory. Use it to show short names in dialogs and reports or to build related names.

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: Full or relative file name.

tools.notes: filename is a builtin, so it cannot be used as a variable name.

tools.name: filesetext
tools.description: Returns the given file name with its extension replaced by a new one. It is the standard way to derive output file names from the design name, for example B.name to a .csv or .scr file in the same directory.

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: Original file name.

parameters.name: newext
parameters.description: New extension including the leading dot, e.g. ".txt".

tools.notes: Include the dot in newext (".txt"). Passing "" removes the extension. Writing to a .brd/.sch/.lbr name with output() needs mode "F".

tools.name: filesize
tools.description: Returns the size of a file in bytes. Useful to check that an expected input exists and is not empty, or to report file sizes in listings created with fileglob().
tools.notes: See filetime() for the modification time.

tools.name: filetime
tools.description: Returns the timestamp of a file in seconds, in the same format as time(), so it can be formatted with t2string() or compared with other timestamps. Use it to show when a design was last saved or to detect outdated output files.
tools.notes: Combine with t2string(t, "yyyy-MM-dd hh:mm") for readable output.

tools.name: fileread
tools.description: Reads a file into a variable and returns the number of objects read. The destination type selects the mode: a char array receives raw bytes (return value = file size), a string array receives one text line per element without newline characters (return value = number of lines), and a string receives the whole text (return value = its length).
tools.usage: int fileread(dest, string file);   // dest: char[] | string[] | string

parameters.name: dest
parameters.description: char array (binary), string array (lines) or string (entire text).

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: File name to read.

tools.notes: With a string destination the length can differ from the file size when the OS stores CR/LF line ends. Combine with lookup(), strsplit() or the XML functions; check fileerror() for failures.

tools.name: abs
tools.description: Returns the absolute value of a char, int or real value; the result has the same type as the argument. Typical use is computing distances or sizes from coordinate differences.
tools.usage: type abs(type x);     // type: char, int or real
tools.notes: If an argument is invalid, the error message shows the actual argument values.

tools.name: max, min
tools.description: Return the larger or smaller of two values of type char, int or real. The result type is the larger type of the two arguments. They are handy for bounding boxes and running extremes.
tools.usage:
type max(type x, type y);
type min(type x, type y);
tools.notes: Only two arguments; nest calls for more.

tools.name: ceil, floor
tools.description: ceil returns the smallest integral value not less than x, floor the largest integral value not greater than x, both as real. Use them to snap values up or down to a grid or to compute counts that must round up.
tools.usage:
real ceil(real x);
real floor(real x);
tools.notes: The result is real; cast with int() when an integer is needed.

tools.name: round
tools.description: Returns x rounded to the nearest integral value, as real. Use it before converting to int (which would truncate) and for snapping coordinates to a grid.
tools.notes: int(x) truncates; int(round(x)) rounds. To round to decimals use round(x * 100) / 100. MOVE by name only moves elements while the tOrigins/bOrigins layer is visible.

tools.name: trunc, frac
tools.description: trunc returns the integer part of x and frac its fractional part, both as real (x == trunc(x) + frac(x)). Use them to split values, for example into whole millimetres and remainder or degrees and fractions.
tools.usage:
real trunc(real x);
real frac(real x);
tools.example:
real a = 123.75;
printf("%.0f whole, %.2f fraction\n", trunc(a), frac(a));   // 123 whole, 0.75 fraction
tools.notes: trunc rounds toward zero, unlike floor for negative values.

tools.name: sin, cos, tan
tools.description: Trigonometric functions of an angle given in radians, returning real. Use them to rotate points, place parts on a circle or compute arc end points; convert degrees with deg * PI / 180.
tools.notes: Object angles (E.angle, arc angles) are in degrees, so convert before calling these functions.

tools.name: asin, acos, atan
tools.description: Inverse trigonometric functions returning the angle in radians as real. Use them to derive rotation angles from coordinates, e.g. the direction of a wire; multiply by 180 / PI for degrees.
tools.notes: There is only single-argument atan: handle the quadrant and division by zero (vertical lines) yourself. Arguments outside -1..1 for asin/acos produce an error that shows the offending value.

tools.name: exp
tools.description: Returns e raised to the power x as real. Useful for formulas such as exponential derating or RC timing in calculation ULPs.
tools.example:
real R = 10e3, C = 100e-9, t = 1e-3;
real Vc = 5.0 * (1 - exp(-t / (R * C)));   // capacitor voltage after t
tools.notes: See log() for the inverse.

tools.name: log, log10
tools.description: log returns the natural logarithm and log10 the base-10 logarithm of x, as real. Typical uses are decibel calculations and choosing E-series values.
tools.usage:
real log(real x);
real log10(real x);
tools.notes: x must be positive; otherwise the ULP stops with an error such as Invalid argument in call to 'log(0)'.

tools.name: pow
tools.description: Returns x raised to the power y as real. It also provides arbitrary roots, e.g. pow(x, 1.0/3) for the cube root.
tools.notes: 1/3 is an integer division giving 0; use 1.0/3.

tools.name: sqrt
tools.description: Returns the square root of x as real. The usual application is the length of a wire or the distance between two points.
tools.notes: A negative argument stops the ULP with Invalid argument in call to 'sqrt(...)' showing the value. Arcs need W.arc for their true length.

tools.name: cfgget
tools.description: Reads a configuration parameter stored earlier with cfgset() from the user's eaglerc file. If the parameter does not exist, the optional default (or an empty string) is returned. Use it to remember dialog settings, paths or options between runs of a ULP.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Parameter name, e.g. "myulp.LastFile".

parameters.name: default
parameters.description: Value returned if the parameter has not been stored yet.

tools.example:
string OutDir = cfgget("ULP:myexport.OutDir", EAGLE_HOME);
int Quiet = strtol(cfgget("ULP:myexport.Quiet", "0"));
tools.notes: Names may contain A-Z, a-z, 0-9, '.' and '_' and are case-sensitive. Prefix them with the ULP name (e.g. myexport.OutDir) to avoid collisions; the optional "ULP:" prefix is how they are stored. EAGLE's own settings are readable with the prefix "EAGLE:" (e.g. EAGLE:Option.XrefLabelFormat), but they are undocumented.

tools.name: cfgset
tools.description: Stores a configuration parameter (a string value under a name) in the user's eaglerc file so that it can be read again with cfgget() in later sessions. It is the persistent storage for ULP options.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Parameter name (A-Z a-z 0-9 . _), best prefixed with the ULP name.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: String value to store.

tools.notes: Values are strings: convert numbers with sprintf(). Be very careful with "EAGLE:" parameters - they are EAGLE's own settings; some changes only take effect after a restart. With eagle -U- no settings file is read or written.

tools.name: country
tools.description: Returns the two-letter upper-case country code of the system, or "US" if it cannot be determined. Use it to pick regional defaults such as units or date formats.
tools.example:
int UseInch = country() == "US";
dlgMessageBox("Your country code is: " + country());
tools.notes: See language() for the language code used for translated texts.

tools.name: language
tools.description: Returns the two-letter lower-case language code of the system (default "en"). ULPs use it to show translated texts, typically together with lookup() on a table of message strings, and #usage uses the same codes.
tools.notes: The first language in the table should be the one the ULP's strings are written in (normally English); an unknown language falls back to the original text.

tools.name: exit
tools.description: Terminates the ULP immediately. With an int argument that value becomes the program's return value (non-zero stops a calling script). With a string argument, the string is executed as editor commands, as if typed on the command line right after RUN, and the return value is EXIT_SUCCESS - this is how ULPs modify designs.

parameters.name: result
parameters.description: Return value; 0/EXIT_SUCCESS = success, anything else = failure.

parameters.name: command
parameters.description: Editor command string (commands separated by ';') to execute after the ULP ends.

tools.notes: exit() ends the whole program, also from inside functions. For long command sequences write a .scr file with output() and use exit("SCRIPT 'file.scr';"). Commands are executed in the editor window the ULP was started from.

tools.name: fdlsignature
tools.description: Calculates the digital signature needed when accessing Premier Farnell's Design Link interface from a ULP. It is only relevant for that web service integration.
tools.example: string Sig = fdlsignature(RequestString, Key);   // used by the Design Link ULPs
tools.notes: Special-purpose function; the Farnell Design Link service integration is historical.

tools.name: lookup
tools.description: Looks up a record in a string array of delimited records (e.g. read with fileread()) by its key field and returns a field chosen by index or by header name. The first field is the key (index 0); if the first record is a header, fields can be addressed by name. An empty key returns the requested field of the first record, which lets a program check that a header field exists.
tools.usage:
string lookup(string array[], string key, int field_index[, char separator]);
string lookup(string array[], string key, string field_name[, char separator]);

parameters.name: array
parameters.description: Records, one per element.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Value of the first field of the wanted record ("" = first record).

parameters.name: field_index / field_name
parameters.description: Field number (0 = key) or header name.

parameters.name: separator
parameters.description: Field separator, default '\t'.

tools.notes: The default separator is tab, which avoids quoting. With other separators, fields containing the separator must be in double quotes, and embedded quotes are doubled. Keys must be unique and non-empty; a missing key or field returns an empty string.

tools.name: palette
tools.description: Returns the ARGB color value (0xaarrggbb) of a palette entry, or with index -1 the type of the palette used by the current editor window. Use it together with UL_LAYER.color when a ULP draws or exports colored graphics.
tools.usage:
int palette(int index[, int type]);
PALETTE_TYPES (3), PALETTE_BLACK (0), PALETTE_WHITE (1), PALETTE_COLORED (2), PALETTE_ENTRIES (64)

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: Color index 0..63, or -1 to query the palette type.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Palette to use: PALETTE_BLACK, PALETTE_WHITE, PALETTE_COLORED, or -1 for the current one.

tools.notes: index must be 0..PALETTE_ENTRIES-1 (or -1); type is -1/omitted for the current window's palette or one of PALETTE_BLACK, PALETTE_WHITE, PALETTE_COLORED. Out-of-range values terminate the ULP with an error.

tools.name: sleep
tools.description: Delays the execution of the ULP for the given number of seconds. It can be used to wait for an external program or file, for example while polling for a result written by a tool started with system().
tools.notes: The editor does not respond while the ULP sleeps; keep waits short.

tools.name: sort
tools.description: Sorts arrays in place. Called with one array, it sorts that array directly. Called with an int index array followed by one or more data arrays, it leaves the data untouched and fills the index array so that data[index[i]] is in sorted order, with the first data array as primary key, the second as secondary key and so on.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: Number of elements to sort.

parameters.name: array1
parameters.description: Array to sort, or an int index array when more arrays follow.

parameters.name: array2, ...
parameters.description: Data arrays (any array type) used as sort keys in order.

tools.notes: number is the element count to sort. Declare string arrays numeric to get IC1, IC2, ... IC10 instead of IC1, IC10, IC2. The index array must be int; its previous contents are overwritten.

tools.name: status
tools.description: Shows a message in the status bar of the editor window running the ULP. Use it for progress information during long loops without interrupting the user.
tools.notes: For messages that need acknowledgement use dlgMessageBox().

tools.name: system
tools.description: Runs an external program and waits until it ends, returning its exit status (normally 0 for success). ULPs use it to call converters, simulators or scripts on files they have written. Output redirection and background execution need an explicit command processor on Windows.

parameters.name: command
parameters.description: Command line of the external program.

tools.notes: On Linux/macOS use "prog < in > out" and "prog &" for background runs; on Windows use "cmd.exe /c prog < in > out" and "cmd.exe /c start prog". Quote paths with blanks. Consider wrapping calls in a confirmation dialog so the user sees what will be executed.

tools.name: u2mm, mm2u
tools.description: Convert between EAGLE internal units and millimetres. All coordinates and sizes are int values with a resolution of 1/320000 mm; u2mm turns them into real millimetres for output, and mm2u turns millimetre values (e.g. user input) into internal units for comparisons with object members.
tools.usage:
real u2mm(int n);
int  mm2u(real n);
tools.notes: Compare in internal units (ints) rather than in converted reals to avoid rounding issues.

tools.name: u2mil, mil2u
tools.description: Convert between internal units and mil (1/1000 inch). Handy for US-style design rules, drill tables and 0.1 inch symbol grids.
tools.usage:
real u2mil(int n);
int  mil2u(real n);
tools.notes: Internal resolution is 1/320000 mm, so values in mil are generally not exact integers.

tools.name: u2inch, inch2u
tools.description: Convert between internal units and inch. Useful for pick-and-place files or tools that expect inch coordinates and for schematic coordinates, which are usually on an inch-based grid.
tools.usage:
real u2inch(int n);
int  inch2u(real n);
tools.example:
board(B) output(filesetext(B.name, ".mnt"), "wt") B.elements(E)
  printf("%s %.4f %.4f %.0f\n", E.name, u2inch(E.x), u2inch(E.y), E.angle);
tools.notes: 1 inch = 25.4 mm = 8128000 internal units.

tools.name: u2mic, mic2u
tools.description: Convert between internal units and microns (1/1000 mm). Use them where micrometre precision is expected, e.g. for tolerances, plating or fine-pitch analyses.
tools.usage:
real u2mic(int n);
int  mic2u(real n);
tools.notes: One internal unit is 0.003125 micron.
